about.title: Costa Mesa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Costa Mesa sits where SR-55 winds down toward the coast, and a lot of the city's traffic funnels through a handful of arterials on the way there. Public records for 2025 list 619 injury collisions across the city, 847 people hurt, and 4 lives lost. Newport Boulevard and Harbor Boulevard carry the largest share of reported crashes, followed by the southbound and northbound sides of SR-55. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when reports cluster. If one of those numbers is you, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. We handle personal injury claims arising from car accidents in Orange County. Our service is free—we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, and far less if a public agency is involved, so an early conversation matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Costa Mesa Drivers Choose Us

items.title: Deadlines That Sneak Up
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a city, county, or state vehicle is involved. We can sort out which clock applies to your crash before it runs out.

items.title: Partly at Fault? You Still Have a Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being assigned a share of the blame reduces your recovery rather than erasing it. That distinction matters when the other insurer tries to pin the crash on you.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. And because California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car crash cases, the full picture of what you went through can be part of the claim.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my crash on Newport Boulevard. Should I give one?
items.answer: You're not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and it's generally wise not to. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can shrink your claim later. Politely decline, write down what you remember while it's fresh, and let us handle those conversations.

items.question: What should I save after a car accident in Costa Mesa?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of the vehicles and the scene, the police report number, medical records, receipts, and the names of anyone who saw what happened. If your crash was near a business on Harbor Boulevard or another busy street, nearby cameras may have footage, but that video is often overwritten within days. Acting quickly helps preserve it.

items.question: Do you charge me anything, and do you represent me?
items.answer: Our case review is free to use. We handle personal injury claims arising from Orange County car accidents on a contingency basis—you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.
